title: ग्रामर: वाक्य जोड़ना और too ... to
Grammar: vaakya jodna aur too ... to
Grammar in Use: joining sentences and too ... to

card: दो वाक्य who (कौन), which (कौन सा), when (जब), where (जहाँ) से जुड़ते हैं। किताब का उदाहरण: Ranjana wants to buy a book. Ramu has the same book. → Ranjana wants to buy the same book which Ramu has.

Do vaakya who (kaun), which (kaun sa), when (jab), where (jahan) se judte hain. Kitaab ka udaharan: Ranjana wants to buy a book. Ramu has the same book. → Ranjana wants to buy the same book which Ramu has.
Two sentences can be joined with who, which, when or where. The book's example: Ranjana wants to buy a book. Ramu has the same book. → Ranjana wants to buy the same book which Ramu has.

build: जोड़ो (when): Mother went to market. Ramu was sleeping.
Jodo (when): Mother went to market. Ramu was sleeping.
Join with ‘when’: Mother went to market. Ramu was sleeping.

when

Jodo (when): Sona called me. I was reading.

जब मैं पढ़ रहा/रही था/थी, तब सोना ने मुझे बुलाया।

card: ‘too ... to’ = इतना ज़्यादा कि नहीं हो सकता। इसे ‘so ... that ... cannot’ से लिख सकते हैं। Tea is too hot to drink. → Tea is so hot that it cannot be drunk। (drink, drank, drunk)
‘too ... to’ = itna zyaada ki nahi ho sakta. Ise ‘so ... that ... cannot’ se likh sakte hain. Tea is too hot to drink. → Tea is so hot that it cannot be drunk. (drink, drank, drunk)
‘too ... to’ means so much that it can't be done. We can rewrite it with ‘so ... that ... cannot’. Tea is too hot to drink. → Tea is so hot that it cannot be drunk. (drink, drank, drunk)
